name: The young mockers of Bethel
charge: Mocking the prophet of the Lord: go up, thou bald head
summary: As Elisha went up to Bethel, just after the Lord healed Jericho’s waters through him, young children came out of the city and jeered at him, telling him to go up, bald head (2 Kings 2:19-23). He turned, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord, and two she bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of them (2 Kings 2:24). The teaching uses it to warn that God brings every work into judgment, even the works of children, and that elders are to be honored as fathers.
offenseFull: Elisha had just come from Jericho, where the men of the city told him the water was bad and the land barren; he threw salt into the spring and said the Lord had healed the waters (2 Kings 2:19-22). The sign showed that the spirit that had been on Elijah now worked through Elisha, the double portion coming into effect. He was not a man to be played with. From there he went up to Bethel, and as he went up the road, young children came out of the city and mocked him, telling him to go up, bald head (2 Kings 2:23). The baldness shows he had some age on him. They saw a prophet and did not care.

This is the child behaving proudly against the elder, as Isaiah described a people under judgment (Isaiah 3:5). Honor your father and mother, and do not dishonor a man in his old age (Matthew 15:4; Ecclesiasticus 8:6); an elder is to be entreated as a father (1 Timothy 5:1), and the eye that mocks a father the ravens of the valley will pick out (Proverbs 30:17). The elders over the congregation are to be honored as fathers, and these children’s parents had not taught them right. Children disrespecting elders is a sin, and it is the same lack of home training that fills the gangs today. Do not judge a man by his looks; you might be dealing with an Elisha.
judgmentFull: He turned back, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord, and two she bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of the children (2 Kings 2:24). He cursed them in the name of the Lord, so whatever happened next was of the Lord. Two bears could not have caught forty-two children scattering in every direction unless it was a spiritual thing; the Lord put the spirit on those bears. There are spirits created for vengeance, and the teeth of wild beasts are among them (Ecclesiasticus 39:28-30). It is one of the curses of the law on a people who walk contrary to Him, that He will send wild beasts among them to rob them of their children (Leviticus 26:22). The teachers speak of the forty-two as put to death, though the text says only that the bears tore them.

Elisha went on to Mount Carmel and from there returned to Samaria (2 Kings 2:25). God brings every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil (Ecclesiastes 12:14), and that includes the works of children. The teaching charges parents to read these judgments to their children and put the fear of the Lord in them before it is too late. It is a harsh judgment, and one teacher says plainly that we do not know all the Lord’s reasons; the lesson he draws is to leave vengeance to the Lord, whose judgment this was.

text.text: And the men of the city said unto Elisha, Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water is naught, and the ground barren.
And he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought it to him.
And he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.
So the waters were healed unto this day, according to the saying of Elisha which he spake.

And he went up from thence unto Beth–el: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head.
And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.

And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.
For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.
Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us wax old.
Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;
The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.
There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.
Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance;
Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.
I will also send wild beasts among you, which shall rob you of your children, and destroy your cattle, and make you few in number; and your high ways shall be desolate.
And he went from thence to mount Carmel, and from thence he returned to Samaria.
For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

And he went up from thence unto Beth–el: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head.
And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.
And he went from thence to mount Carmel, and from thence he returned to Samaria.
And if ye walk contrary unto me, and will not hearken unto me; I will bring seven times more plagues upon you according to your sins.
I will also send wild beasts among you, which shall rob you of your children, and destroy your cattle, and make you few in number; and your high ways shall be desolate.
Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.
And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.
Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
